title: Descriptor, SQLite authority and user-scoped application service
summary: Separate source/caller/project identity from persistence. Implement transactional SQLite, bounded consistency and complete API-only clients.
description:
Purpose: Every agent uses planner load against one shared service with independent session/context/execution attribution. Separate source/caller/project identity from persistence. Implement transactional SQLite, bounded consistency and complete API-only clients.

Current state: this phase is planned; current production persistence remains JSON until the SQLite/API migration is implemented. Reuse existing capabilities instead of creating another planner.

Deliverables and sole owners:
- P128(F025)/T489: Descriptor-first project and workspace identity independent of code checkout and database location.
- P128(F025)/T502: Transactional SQLite authority with versioned documents, search and durable command receipts.
- P128(F025)/T496: Atomic structural consistency and bounded semantic reconciliation after every mutation.
- P128(F025)/T490: One authenticated multi-project application service used by every supported client: shared runtime location with newest-version launcher (protocol N/N-1), local-only Web UI (loopback with Host/Origin checks, pluggable auth middleware), audit-only planner writes and the execution lock (in-progress / parked / abandoned).

Execution contract:
Follow the task dependencies and the phase priority in the rebuilt F025 plan. Keep coherent phase work and recover approved detours; do not introduce a global task queue or silently preempt active work. Use the user-scoped service/SQLite boundary, explicit workspace identity, complete bounded context and revision-bound evidence wherever applicable.

Acceptance:
Each task proves its stated outcome; preserve IDs/history, single-owner decisions and phase handoffs. Mechanical parent/dependency effects are consistent; semantic review is factual, reviewed-unchanged or explicitly pending. Native/provider/installed claims need their actual owner evidence.

tasks.title: Separate planner storage, code workspace and runtime identities
tasks.description:
Outcome: Descriptor-first project and workspace identity independent of code checkout and database location.

Current implementation: Consumers default to cwd/.planner or AGENT_PLAN_ROOT; code root is inferred from the planner directory. git-common-dir currently supports allocation, not portable identity.

Implementation responsibility:
- Finalize a versioned descriptor and resolver precedence for explicit selection, nested repositories, non-Git/empty folders and copied/forked descriptors.
- Define resolver/registration ports and stable project/workspace/caller bindings; keep path/branch mutable and native session separate from planner ownership.
- Resolve descriptor first, legacy migration second, initialization last. Incompatible descriptor or missing bound data yields typed errors; never create a silent replacement.
- Define the service-owned HOME location and git-common-dir as local clone evidence only. Supply typed registration interfaces for the SQLite and service owners without opening a client-side store.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Two worktrees bind one project and distinct source contexts; non-Git planning and undecided languages remain valid.
- Moving a folder/renaming a branch preserves identity; ambiguous forks/foreign overrides require deliberate rebind.
- Descriptor contains no secrets, database path or live sessions; deletion of HOME leads to restore-required.

(C2) resolver/registration ports typed for the downstream owners without opening any client-side store: WorkspaceResolution (descriptor | descriptor-error | legacy | none), RepositoryRegistration (projectId + cloneKey + stored same-project/new-project BindDecision + registeredAt — the once-asked fork/copy question), WorkspaceRegistration (workspaceId+projectId with mutable path/branch locators), ProjectStoreRegistration (T502 port: service-owned store location) and ServiceEndpointRecord (T490 port: protocolVersion+bootId+host/port, matching the verify-don't-trust rule; plan-server's server-record.ts remains the runtime precedent). (C3) one resolver for every client, resolvePlannerWorkspace: nearest descriptor walking up wins (nested monorepo sub-project beats ancestor — tested), the walk never crosses a repository boundary without a descriptor (tested with a real git repo), legacy .planner resolves as the migration-offer state, an empty folder resolves none (initialization offer, valid state), and an unreadable or incompatible descriptor is surfaced as typed descriptor-error instead of a silent fallback; readProjectDescriptor returns PROJECT_DESCRIPTOR_INVALID (broken JSON, strict-schema violation) or PROJECT_DESCRIPTOR_INCOMPATIBLE (foreign schemaVersion with foundSchemaVersion attached, never migrated silently). (C4) HOME location stays service-owned (no client path in the descriptor by schema construction); cloneKeyFor derives the clone key from git --git-common-dir including worktree pointer files, as local clone evidence only — verified with two worktrees of one fixture clone: same projectId, same clone key (realpath-normalized), distinct source roots. (C5) acceptance evidence: non-Git folder with snapshot valid; copied folder carrying the known projectId surfaces it for the deliberate rebind; atomic write round-trips through the strict schema. Unverified boundaries recorded: consumers still infer cwd/.planner until T490 routes them (dated, observable behavior unchanged — no rewiring in this task); restore-required flow on missing HOME data is T495/T490 work; no SQLite store exists yet so registration ports are interfaces, verified as types at build, not runtime. No real project, migration, dashboard or Git publication touched; all fixtures mkdtemp and cleaned up.

Workspace identity is inferred from process cwd — the T461 baseline captured this live (AGENT_PLAN_ROOT unset -> cwd/.planner).

- packages/agent-plan/src/index.ts:125 — CLI default root `join(cwd, '.planner')` plus a --root flag; init/serve/stop all operate on the passed root; no descriptor awareness.
- packages/plan-server/src/server-record.ts:39-82 — runtime service registration lives at <planRoot>/.local/server.json (ServerRecord read/validated; pid+port based). This is the runtime-record precedent: an advertised local record that callers must verify, not trust by pid/port alone — exactly the pattern architecture.md §2 prescribes for the service boot record.
- packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:504-527 gitCommonDirFor(planRoot) walks up from the plan root reading .git (dir or worktree pointer file) to the common dir; used at line ~1758 by allocateEntityIdentity: worktrees of one clone share `.git/agent-plan/allocations/<manifest.projectId>.json` guarded by a cross-process write lock, reserving F/P/T numbers and 5-char shortIds before entity files are written. So git-common-dir is ALREADY clone-level coordination evidence for allocation — but identity itself comes from the .planner manifest, which is inside the mutable planner folder and does not survive a descriptor-less copy binding.
- packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts:71-73 — ManifestSchema { schemaVersion: literal(1), projectId: string.min(1), ... } persisted at <root>/manifest.json (plan-store.ts:1340, loadManifest 1705). The projectId already exists as a stable planner identity; what is missing is its portability OUTSIDE the planner folder and the resolver precedence (descriptor -> legacy -> init) plus typed fork/copy binding decisions.

Precedents and relevance: architecture.md §3 defines the proposed descriptor (.agent-plan.json, schemaVersion, projectId, snapshot{remote,branch}), the binding decision (worktrees of a registered clone bind automatically; other projectId-carrying folders asked once: same project vs new project, answer stored, rebind explicit), and the 6-step resolver order; decisions.md fixes the same. The T461 baseline supplies the failure evidence the implementation must remove: missing descriptor = workspace undetectable (exists() false), incompatible schemaVersion rejected without migration, cwd inference as the only identity source. gitCommonDirFor is the one existing git-based identity helper and is reused as local clone evidence only (never a network/remote identity).

Reuse and ownership: the descriptor schema/reader/resolver go into ONE new core module (packages/plan-core/src/project-descriptor.ts) consumed later by plan-mcp/pi-adapter/CLI/plan-server through T490's routing; T502/T490 implement the service/SQLite registration ports typed here. Zod + literal schemaVersion + strict object (no passthrough: no secrets/db paths/live agents can survive parsing) follows ManifestSchema conventions and the project-context fingerprint pattern. Tests use mkdtemp fixtures per AGENTS.md rule 17 (never a real project). No consumer rewiring, no real migration, no Git publication in this task.

tasks.title: Route all clients through one coordinated local planner authority
tasks.description:
Outcome: One authenticated multi-project application service used by every supported client.

Current implementation: MCP/Pi construct PlanStore directly; v1 is GET-only and Web UI routes have separate behavior. Server records are advisory and per root. plan-server uses cors({origin:"*"}) without authentication. Task ownership never expires, so a task left by a switch blocks a later resume.

Implementation responsibility:
- Each agent enters through planner load: descriptor resolution, shared-service reuse, independent registration and complete applicable context (docs/agent-brain/session-registration.md). Dashboard presentation is separate; simultaneous loads must not spawn HTTP servers or browsers.
- Distribution: Heca's bundle and npm installs both place service versions under ~/.agent-plan/runtime/<version>/. The user-scoped launcher atomically starts the newest installed version; the service accepts protocol N and N-1; MCP/Pi bridges are thin, version-tolerant clients. A newer installed version takes over once no write is in progress. No first-starter-wins incompatibility; lifetime is not tied to a window.
- Expose a complete versioned application API over the shared SQLite/domain boundary: current CRUD/discuss, requirements/decisions, lifecycle, handoffs, documents/search, context and recovery operations. Preserve v1 compatibility explicitly.
- Convert MCP into its stdio API bridge, Pi into its native API adapter, and CLI/Web UI into the same operations. Inventory actual tool/error/approval parity before removing direct store access.
- Local access without a token: listen only on 127.0.0.1; reject Host headers other than localhost/127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding); accept writes and WebSocket upgrades only from the Agent Plan UI and Heca origins; remove cors({origin:"*"}) and the LAN mode.
- Prepare remote use without building it: one authentication middleware with pluggable strategies (today loopback + Host/Origin, later per-device tokens issued by pairing); every request resolves a principalId recorded in the audit; permissions come from the principal, never from the request being local.
- Planner writes are not restricted between agents: workers and orchestrators may modify other tasks on request. Record actor and requester on every mutation (audit) instead of blocking; no role- or room-based write gates.
- Execution lock, the only block: in-progress blocks a start by another live session; parked (switch/return) does not block, a takeover warns, is recorded and the original session is told on return; abandoned when the adapter heartbeat (about every 30 s, in code) stops, the lease expiring about 2 min after process death without manual recovery. The same logical agent (same Heca member, or same harness + workspace when standalone) reclaims its tasks. A live owner idle beyond a configurable threshold (e.g. 2 h) is shown idle; takeover only with explicit confirmation. The Web UI offers a human Release action.
- Bootstrap snapshots and project-filtered WebSocket events using durable cursors/outbox with bounded replay, gap/epoch handling and slow-consumer limits. Serve the correct source workspace independently of data root.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Concurrent clients observe one authority; only one live session can hold the in-progress lock of a task.
- A killed agent's task becomes abandoned within the lease; the same agent reclaims it; another agent takes over an idle task only after confirmation.
- Different projects/worktrees keep independent context/returns/overlays; API clients never open the DB.
- Every existing operation remains reachable; no silent cwd fallback, auto dashboard or separate per-project service.
- Requests with a foreign Host or Origin, cross-site writes and non-loopback connections are rejected; Heca-bundled and npm-installed versions converge on the newest service.
- Lost acknowledgements, stale revisions, unavailable service and incompatible clients have typed non-success results.

tasks.title: Reconcile affected hierarchy and dependencies with bounded context cost
tasks.description:
Outcome: Atomic structural consistency and bounded semantic reconciliation after every mutation.

Current implementation: Parent rollups, reference validation and description freshness exist. Their separate file-based paths do not yet provide the full affected-context postcondition through the new service.

Implementation responsibility:
- Use SQLite reverse indexes to determine old/new parents, requirement links and real dependency consumers for create/update/move/dependency operations.
- Commit mechanical membership/status/reference consequences with the leaf mutation; issue compact version-bound impact receipts.
- For semantic prose and decision applicability, support explicit factual updates, reviewed-unchanged evidence or durable reconciliation_required obligations. Never blindly copy child text upward.
- Reject stale/cyclic/foreign reconciliation; paginate genuine high-fan-out work and preserve pending obligations after crashes.
- Cover project/feature/phase/task updates, new tasks, moves across features and dependencies without a full-plan or full-ancestor reread per operation.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A leaf save cannot report complete reconciliation while relevant obligations remain.
- Unrelated plan growth and repeated no-op updates do not cause unconditional full context delivery.
- Requirements/decisions keep their canonical single owners and measured budgets never omit mandatory information.

**Completion summary:**
Shipped: bounded semantic reconciliation over the SQLite authority. (C1) reconcileLeafMutation answers the affected-context question from reverse indexes only — affected parents including BOTH sides of a task move (previousPhaseId + current membership join), requirement links via entity_requirements, and real dependency consumers via the reverse dependency index — with no full-plan or full-ancestor reread per operation, verified by the 9-test suite. tasks.description:
Outcome: Transactional SQLite authority with versioned documents, search and durable command receipts.

Current implementation: PlanStore uses multi-file JSON and root locks. The service-owned SQLite backend selected by the user has no dedicated implementation owner; current exports are not a full portable database backup.

Implementation responsibility:
- Choose the driver by benchmark: node:sqlite (built-in, no native addon) versus better-sqlite3 (native addon, expected faster) on real planner flows (start/claim, context load, FTS search, bulk import, backup), on the latest Node release available when this task starts. Put the winner behind a thin, harness-independent persistence-driver interface. Heca bundles that pinned Node runtime; npm installs declare it as the minimum; if better-sqlite3 wins, ship prebuilt binaries per OS/CPU. Verify FTS5, JSON, WAL, the backup API and crash behaviour on the pinned build. Keep blocking DB work in a bounded worker and document schema/driver compatibility.
- Implement relational entity/parent/dependency/ownership/revision tables, validated extensible JSON metadata, single-owner decision revisions, logical document folders/content/assets and indexed reverse relationships.
- Implement BEGIN IMMEDIATE command transactions with expected revisions, authenticated caller identity, idempotency-key/payload validation, durable receipt and outbox/event cursor committed together. No Git/network/model calls in a transaction.
- Provide document CRUD/history, exact-ID/literal and FTS5 word/phrase search with filters, snippets and pagination. Maintain a rebuildable FTS index transactionally; clients receive content through domain operations, never SQL or DB paths.
- Enable foreign keys and a reviewed WAL/durability/busy/checkpoint policy. Expose consistent snapshot/backup primitives and schema migration APIs for T494/T495; no live JSON/Markdown mirror.
- Measure representative read/context/write/search flows and inject before-commit, after-commit/lost-ack and event-publication crashes in temporary fixtures.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Task/parent/receipt/event state commits atomically; retry of a retained request cannot repeat the mutation, and conflicting payload reuse is refused.
- Tasks are independent rows; documents/required portable assets survive snapshot restore and FTS can be rebuilt without changing canonical content.
- SQLite is embedded in Agent Plan only; no separate DB service, network filesystem DB or installed user-data migration.
- The backend provides complete typed primitives for T496/T490 and exposes honest busy/corrupt/schema-incompatible outcomes.

- snapshot.ts: openStore (missing file without create → typed UNAVAILABLE; verification before any domain call, close-once), createSnapshot via VACUUM INTO, restoreFromSnapshot + schema verify for T494/T495.
